LESSON: WORD CLASSES: CONJUNCTIONS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Word Classes: Conjunctions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Word Classes: Conjunctions, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: Why do you join words and sentences? 2. How do you join words or sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Word Classes: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify conjunctions: but, or, yet, because, since and also, in texts for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Word Classes: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use conjunctions but, or, yet, because, since and also, correctly in communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Word Classes: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. judge the correctness and appropriateness of conjunctions in oral, signed and written texts. • In groups, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or signed video clip with vocabulary related to leisure time activities. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and articulate signs of vocabulary related to leisure time activities • In groups, learners who are Hard of Hearing are guided to listen to a short signed dialogue and identify conjunctions. • In groups, learners who are Deaf are guided to observe a short signed dialogue and identify conjunctions. • In pairs, learners are guided to make and sign sentences, from a substitution table using but, or, yet, because, since and also. • In pairs, learners are guided to construct sentences using conjunctions. • Individually, learners are guided to fill in blank spaces using conjunctions in sentences or paragraphs. 1. Why do you join words and sentences? 2. How do you join words or sentences? 90 • In pairs, learners are guided to create a display chart of sentences containing conjunctions. • In groups, learners are guided to conduct a gallery walk and give feedback to each other’s work.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Word Classes: Conjunctions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: Learning Independently as learners, individually, fill in blank spaces using conjunctions in sentences or paragraphs

• Critical thinking and problem solving: Open mindedness and creativity as learners give feedback to each other’s work after conducting a gallery

walk.

• Communication and Collaboration: Articulating signs clearly as learners, in pairs or groups, observe, fingerspell and sign words related to the

theme; leisure time activities

Values:
Love: Sharing as learners display chart of sentences containing conjunctions to their peers.

Link to other Subjects:

Learners are able to relate the knowledge of the use of conjunctions to their learning in Kiswahili .
